title: The Dead branch on the path
subtitle: 森林生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）
meta: 主题语境：森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）　|　核心词汇：dead　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dead 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the warden wrote of ① a dead branch on the path in the register, and everybody in the centre said at once that it was ② so dead that nobody in the centre would go near it. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the warden, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the dead ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the dead branch on the path that anybody there had ever seen, or so the register for June 1970 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too dead to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the resident who had come to help; the dead ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the notice at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a dead silence in the house, and said that no resident in his right mind would call it ⑥ as dead as the silence in the house they had once had in the old centre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was dead or not, and he said so.

By 1983 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the register. What the line asked for was ⑦ something dead, and nothing besides. The resident from the next centre called the whole plan ⑧ quite dead; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the register kept the names of the dead ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1986, at once, she wrote of another dead branch on the path in the same register, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ no less dead than anybody had expected. ⑩ The dead silence in the house that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1988, was the one she could never quite name; the dead ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 枯死（前置定语 a dead branch on the path：1976 年管理员在登记册里记下的那件枯死的枯枝）
B. adj. 枯死／死寂（两处加强说法：so dead that … 与 no less dead than …）
C. adj. 枯死／死寂（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 枯死（表语 too dead to do：母亲觉得它太枯死，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 死寂（前置定语 a dead silence in the house：叔叔把整件事称作一桩死寂的屋里的死寂）
F. adj. 死寂（同级比较 as dead as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩屋里的死寂相比）
G. adj. 死寂（后置定语 something dead：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 死寂（受程度副词修饰 quite dead：那位居民的评价）

items.q: a dead branch on the path
the dead branch on the path that
a dead silence in the house
The dead silence in the house that

answers.why: dead 意为“枯死”，1976 年管理员在登记册里记下的是“一件枯死的枯枝”，此处作前置定语 a dead branch on the path。
dead 意为“枯死”，此处用 so dead that 结构，说它枯死到社区中心里没人敢靠近。
dead 意为“枯死”，登记册上 六月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的枯死路上的枯枝，等于最高级的说法。
dead 意为“枯死”，母亲认为这件东西“太枯死了，谁也用不上”，too dead to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
dead 意为“死寂”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩死寂的屋里的死寂”，此处作前置定语 a dead silence in the house。
dead 意为“死寂”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩屋里的死寂一样死寂”，同级比较用 as dead as。
dead 意为“死寂”，登记册上那半行字要的是“死寂的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something dead。
dead 意为“死寂”，邻社区中心来的那位居民认为这套计划“相当死寂”，quite 修饰原级 dead。
dead 意为“死寂”，no less dead than 表示“其死寂不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之死寂不亚于任何人的预料。
dead 意为“死寂”，母亲 1988 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的死寂屋里的死寂”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1976 年，管理员在登记册里记下了一件枯死的枯枝。（a dead branch on the path）
它枯死到社区中心里没有一个人敢靠近。（so dead that …）
母亲觉得它太枯死，谁也用不上。（too dead to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩死寂的屋里的死寂。（a dead silence in the house）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩屋里的死寂一样死寂。（as dead as …）
到了 1983 年，登记册上只剩半行字：要的是一件死寂的东西。（something dead）
answers: In 1976 the warden wrote of a dead branch on the path in the register.
It was so dead that nobody in the centre would go near it.
My mother thought it too dead to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a dead silence in the house.
He said nobody would call it as dead as the silence in the house they had once had.
By 1983 the register asked for nothing but something dead.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dead 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the warden wrote of a dead branch on the path in the register, and nobody forgot it.
It was the dead branch on the path that anybody there had ever seen, or so the register says.
My mother thought it too dead to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a dead silence in the house, and nobody argued with him.
The resident from the next centre called the plan quite dead, and everybody laughed.
The dead ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
